page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache, supporting standard instructions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA. Hardware acceleration is absent, with 0 GPUs included. The instance incorporates 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, while offering no bundled local storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate modest computational and memory throughput capabilities relative to peer instances. Synthetic evaluation shows a Geekbench single-core score of 915.0 and multi-core score of 1993.0, both placing in the bottom 10%. PassMark results follow a similar pattern with a CPU score of 3551.12 and a memory score of 1512.31. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 19.83 GB/sec for large-block reads and 18.72 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific metrics show Redis achieving 2.92 million SET operations per second, static web serving throughput reaching 2.25 GB/sec, and compression speeds of 18.97 GB/sec for gzip and 13.02 GB/sec for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The primary operational tradeoff of the ecs.u0.c1m8.xlarge is the balance between low per-core execution speeds and an expanded memory footprint. While the older Intel Xeon 8163 microarchitecture yields weaker raw computing throughput, the high 8 GB per vCPU ratio makes it cost-efficient for memory-dense tasks that do not saturate processing units. The instance is suitable for lightweight in-memory caching, staging databases, test-environment analytics, and low-traffic background jobs that require substantial memory allocation without high compute demand.
